body.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal Z\ne\varnothing\), \(m\) is odd, every arrow \(j\to i\) in \(G\) satisfies \(j<i\), \(u\to v\in G\), and
\[
 \kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}.
\]
Then the derivative-separated regular class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) is nonempty.  Uniformly over this class, as \(n\to\infty\), the real vector stacking the real and imaginary parts of
\[
 \sqrt n\bigl(\widehat h_{uv}(z)-h_{uv}(z)\bigr),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal Z,
\]
converges to the centered Gaussian law obtained by applying the Jacobian of the moment-to-root recursion and
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}
\]
to the long-run Gaussian lag-moment covariance.  Let \(\widehat\Sigma_h\) be the positive-semidefinite plug-in estimate obtained from the Gaussian Isserlis covariance series and the recursive Jacobian, and let \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the maximum complex modulus of the corresponding centered Gaussian vector.  Then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}}
 \left|
 P\!\left\{
 h_{uv}(z)\in
 \left\{w\in\mathbb C:
 |w-\widehat h_{uv}(z)|\le
 \frac{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}
 \text{ for every }z\in\mathcal Z
 \right\}-(1-\alpha)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the class in the supremum has the full argument list displayed above.
body.justification: The globally separated theorem is preserved as a simple nonvacuous corollary of the sharper target-corridor result.
body.gap: Global regularity is stronger than the target requires, but remains an easily stated sufficient condition.
body.consumer: Existing implementations that already recover the full triangular root may continue to use the global estimator and obtain the same target bands.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}
 =\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}
 (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)
\]
and let
\[
 \mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}
 =\mathcal M_{uv,\mathrm{cor}}^{\partial}
 (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa).
\]
We first verify that the assertion is nonvacuous and that the theorem for
\(\mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}\) applies.  By
\(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}class}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}regular\mbox{-}class}\),
every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}\) belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\), the integer
\(m\) is odd, and
\[
 m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\geq\kappa\quad(i\in V),
 \qquad
 |C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})|\geq\kappa\quad(j\to i\in E).
 \tag{1}
\]
The definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\mbox{-}corridor}\) gives
\(V_{uv}^{G}\subseteq V\) and \(E_{uv}^{G}\subseteq E\).  Restricting the
two finite families of inequalities in \((1)\) to these subsets and using
\(\mathrm{def{:}corridor\mbox{-}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}class}\)
therefore yields
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The hypotheses of the present theorem include the hypotheses of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}nonempty}\),
and its numerical condition is
\(\kappa\leq m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}\).  That lemma consequently gives
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}\neq\varnothing.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the supremum in the claimed coverage statement is not over an empty
class.

We next compare the global and corridor estimators.  The global recursion in
\(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}estimator}\) and the corridor recursion in
\(\mathrm{def{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}recursion}\) use the same real
odd-root operation on every diagonal coordinate in \(V_{uv}^{G}\).  Process
the corridor edges in increasing endpoint gap.  For a corridor edge
\(j\to i\),
\(\mathrm{lem{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}recursion\mbox{-}closure}\)
states that every diagonal coordinate and every strict edge entering
\(R_{ij,m}\) is in the corridor and that each such strict edge has smaller
endpoint gap.  Induction over the endpoint gap therefore shows that the two
recursions have the same remainder, numerator, and denominator at every
corridor update.  Hence, whenever both recursions are defined,
\[
 \widehat A^{\mathrm{global}}_{ij}
 =\widehat A^{\mathrm{cor}}_{ij}
 \quad(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G}),
 \qquad
 \widehat A^{\mathrm{global}}_{ii}
 =\widehat A^{\mathrm{cor}}_{ii}
 \quad(i\in V_{uv}^{G}).
 \tag{4}
\]
Because \(u,v\in V_{uv}^{G}\) and \(u\to v\in E_{uv}^{G}\), substitution
of the coordinates \((v,u)\) and \((v,v)\) from \((4)\) into the transfer
formula gives
\[
 \widehat h_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{\widehat A^{\mathrm{global}}_{vu}z}
 {1-\widehat A^{\mathrm{global}}_{vv}z}
 =\frac{\widehat A^{\mathrm{cor}}_{vu}z}
 {1-\widehat A^{\mathrm{cor}}_{vv}z}
 =\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{cor}}(z),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal Z.
 \tag{5}
\]

On \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\), all population diagonal-root derivatives and
all population divided differences used by the global recursion have
absolute value at least \(\kappa>0\), by \((1)\).  The uniform moment
consistency underlying
\(\mathrm{thm{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}band}\), continuity
of matrix inversion at \(M_0\succ0\), and the finite recursive composition
therefore imply that, uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}\), the
probability tends to one that all empirical diagonal derivatives and divided
differences used by the global recursion have absolute value at least
\(\kappa/2\).  Denote this common regularity event by \(\mathcal E_n\).  Thus
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P(\mathcal E_n^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{6}
\]
and \((5)\) holds on \(\mathcal E_n\).  Arbitrary definitions of either
estimator off \(\mathcal E_n\) cannot affect a uniform weak limit or a
coverage probability, by \((6)\).

The same induction also proves equality as rational maps on the common
regular neighborhood, not merely equality at the observed argument.
Differentiating that identity shows that the target rows of the global and
corridor Jacobians agree.  Since the corridor expression contains no
off-corridor coordinate, its derivatives with respect to all such coordinates
are zero.  The transfer differential is, directly from the quotient rule,
\[
 \mathrm d h_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
 +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}.
 \tag{7}
\]
The denominators in \((7)\) are nonzero because the stability margin gives
\(|A_{vv}z|\leq1-\gamma<1\) for \(z\in\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb T\).
It follows that the global delta-method covariance restricted to the stacked
target vector equals the corridor covariance.  Applying the identical
recursive Jacobian to the same positive-semidefinite Isserlis-series covariance
estimate also gives, on \(\mathcal E_n\),
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_h=\widehat\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{cor}},
 \qquad
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}
 =\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{cor}}.
 \tag{8}
\]

Now apply
\(\mathrm{thm{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}band}\).  Its
hypotheses hold by the hypotheses of the present theorem, and \((2)\) permits
restriction of every uniform assertion from \(\mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}\) to
\(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\).  Equations \((5)\)--\((8)\) then replace the
corridor estimator, covariance, and critical value by their global
counterparts without changing the uniform limit.  This proves the asserted
centered Gaussian limit with differential \((7)\).  Finally, if
\(C_n^{\mathrm{cor}}(P)\) and \(C_n^{\mathrm{global}}(P)\) denote the two
simultaneous-coverage events, then \((5)\) and \((8)\) give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \left|P\!\left(C_n^{\mathrm{global}}(P)\right)
       -P\!\left(C_n^{\mathrm{cor}}(P)\right)\right|
 \leq
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P(\mathcal E_n^c)
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Combining this display with the corridor theorem and the inclusion \((2)\)
gives exactly
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \left|P\!\left(C_n^{\mathrm{global}}(P)\right)-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the claimed simultaneous Wald coverage.
